core_obligations: Use that Z coproduct X' -> X is a ph covering to write F(X) as an equalizer out of F(Z coproduct X') (proof lines 10892-10896).
Expand the fibre product and translate the sheaf condition into pairs (t, s') with t|_E = s'|_E and s' an equalizer element (proof lines 10898-10912).
Remove the equalizer condition using the surjective proper morphism E x_Z E coproduct X' -> X' x_X X' (proof lines 10914-10918).

difficulty_reason: For a sheaf F on the site (Sch/S)_{ph}, the lemma asserts that for any blow up square in that category the resulting square with entries F(E), F(X'), F(Z), F(X) is cartesian in the category of sets (statement lines 10877-10890). The proof notes that Z coproduct X' -> X is a surjective proper morphism, hence a ph covering by Topologies, Lemma labelled topologies-lemma-surjective-proper-ph, so the singleton family computes F(X) as an equalizer of two maps out of F(Z coproduct X') (proof lines 10892-10896). Expanding the fibre product as Z coproduct E coproduct E coproduct (X' x_X X') and using that F is a Zariski sheaf, hence sends disjoint unions to products, the proof rewrites the sheaf condition as the description of F(X) as the set of pairs (t, s') with t|_E = s'|_E and s' in the equalizer of the two maps F(X') -> F(X' x_X X') (proof lines 10898-10912). Finally the morphism E x_Z E coproduct X' -> X' x_X X' is surjective and proper because b induces an isomorphism X' minus E -> X minus Z, so F(X' x_X X') -> F(E x_Z E) x F(X') is injective and the equalizer condition follows from the diagonal one (proof lines 10914-10918). Eliminating the redundant second sheaf condition by exhibiting a second ph covering is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
